body:
**The year the analysis is complete and the man is waiting tables in
Manhattan.** 2023 has 159 originals and they are the most sophisticated writing
on the account: Marxist class analysis stated in its own vocabulary, two
conspiracy theories worked to a resolution and published as negatives, four
tweets forecasting AI deepfakes in elections two years before his own AI turn,
and a running set of dated political predictions he scores out loud when they
fail.

It is also the year he mentions, in passing, that he works at an outdoor-only
restaurant in New York.

## He names Balloon Boy himself, fourteen years later

During the OceanGate Titan submersible disaster — nine posts across 20 and
21 June, a full return to the Sandy-era liveblogging mode — he wrote:

> *"This is so much better than balloon boy."*

[[wiki/self/twitter/2009]] reads the 15 October 2009 Balloon Boy day as the
earliest instance of Dan watching the coverage rather than the event, and files
it as the weaker, undeclared version of the disposition
[[wiki/mind/synthesis/millennial-digital-witness]] describes. **He classifies it
the same way, unprompted, fourteen years later, and uses it as the unit of
comparison for a new spectacle.** That is independent confirmation from the
only person who could give it: Balloon Boy is a landmark in his own taxonomy of
media events, not just in the wiki's.

The OceanGate posts themselves are the mature form of the habit — the old
website mined for *"high weirdness"*, a claim from the company checked against
prior divers' accounts and called *"a straight up lie"*, Stockton Rush's own
words about deep-water fossil-fuel extraction retrieved, a ChatGPT-generated
poem about the disaster posted as evidence of the model's tastelessness, and a
joke submersible business proposed to visit the wreck of the submersible.

## Nashville: two conspiracies, worked, and both published as negatives

**29–30 March.** [[wiki/mind/synthesis/vertical-authority-skepticism]] already
carries this as his most-read tweet ever. The full sequence is the method:

> *"Dumb conspiracy. Shooter does not have Puma's on."*
> *"Disappointed to announce that the 'Audrey Hale shoes' conspiracy is a bust.
> It's not totally clear that the Vans in the CCTV are the same ones in the
> Nashville PD bodycam, but I'm going to go…"*
> *"The second #nashville conspiracy involves the camo pattern on the shooters
> pants and is only slightly more questionable than the shoes."*
> *"For the record, the pattern looks slightly different but not enough to rule
> out the possibility that the difference in lighting and camera resolutions
> wouldn't be the most likely cause of the visual…"*

Two separate theories, both taken seriously enough to check, both **falsified
and published as falsified** — and the second one is rejected on an explicitly
stated confound: lighting and camera resolution as the more likely explanation
than a substitution. He is *"disappointed"*, says so, and reports it anyway.

The complication, and it should be on the record: on **10 February** he
describes himself as *"a conspiracy crank like myself"*. The wiki's finding is
that the label is contradicted by his behaviour; he applies it to himself
ironically, in the middle of laughing at a theory he finds too stupid to
entertain. Both things are true and the self-description does not overturn the
behavioural finding — but a page arguing that a label does not fit should say
that the subject uses it.

## The class analysis arrives, in its own vocabulary

The four-stage sequence on [[wiki/mind/synthesis/2020-left-turn]] turns on an
absence: through 2011–2019 there is no redistributive or class content
anywhere. **3 March 2023 is where that absence closes completely:**

> *"I think people misunderstand that most of bourgeois fear nothing more than
> the loss of class status, even if it would have no negative impact on their
> lives and wellbeing."*
> *"Capitalism in its current form breeds this meaningless psychological
> framework, creating a desire to protect the systemic advantages you enjoy at
> the expense of the real material well-being of everyone…"*
> *"Bourgeois privilege is inseparable from dangerous and completely imaginary
> essentialism. 'When you're accustomed to privilege, equality feels like
> oppression'"*

*Bourgeois*, *class status*, *systemic advantages*, *material well-being* —
and, crucially, the argument is **psychological**: he explains a class position
by the fear of losing it rather than by its economic interest. That is the
anomaly-detection habit applied to political economy, which is what his version
of this politics was always going to look like.

He also keeps policing his own side, harder than in 2022 — *"PSA for tankies -
the trick where you call yourself a 'Marxist-Leninist' to disguise your
objectively far right ideology lost its effect in like 2017"* (15 February),
and on Hasan Piker again: *"How is it that Hasan can be so good at domestic
political analysis and so cringe during every global conflict?"* (14 October).

## AI, two years early, in three registers

**27 May**, a four-post thread on deepfakes and elections:

> *"AI deepfake tools are already convincing enough to the vast majority of the
> population…in their absolute infancy. Their output will improve at
> exponential scale."*
> *"How does the public respond to a scandalous video of a candidate that can't
> be disproven in the heat of a competitive election?"*
> *"Anyone who thinks we can seriously regulate or criminalize emerging tech
> like this is living in fantasyland. Just like p2p file sharing in the 00's,
> Pandora's box is open."*

**13 June**: *"Here's the encrypted message #GPT had me send to Bard"* — a
model-to-model experiment, run and documented, in June 2023.

**21 June**: ChatGPT prompted to write about OceanGate and the output posted as
evidence of the model's judgement (*"Very insensitive #ChatGPT thought
#OceanGate was good poetry material"*).

[[wiki/self/concepts/chatgpt]] dates hands-on model use to the September 2022
DALL·E posts. This is the year after: forecasting the technology's political
consequences, running cross-model experiments, and using the output as material
— **two years before the April 2025 turn that produced this wiki.** The
interest is not new in 2025. What is new in 2025 is turning it on himself.

## Reading, quantified

**2 February**: *"Politics has been so boring that I've plowed through a
cumulative 92 hours of history audiobooks over the last 2 months using only my
monthly audible credit."*

Ninety-two hours in about sixty days — roughly an hour and a half every day,
sustained. The 2018 line was *"my goal in life is to one day be described as a
'voracious reader'"*; this is that goal met and measured, five years later, and
reported as what he does when politics is dull rather than as an achievement.
It is also the volume of input behind the 2024 Roman-history material
[[wiki/interests/roman-republic]] documents.

## The job, one clause again

**2 March**:

> *"I work at an outdoor only NYC restaurant and boy, let me tell you - New
> Yorkers fucking hate these things. They love to tell me all about it as
> though I own the business and built the shack myself."*

The same construction as 2022's *"Wheels are falling waiting tables"* — the
employment is the setting for an observation about customers, never the
subject. It also puts him in Manhattan, which with *"Greatest city on earth"*
(6 April), *"Guten morgen, New York"* (26 June) and the Madison Avenue
installations (18 June) makes 2023 the account's clearest post-2019 location
signal.

## Predictions, and one he scores against himself

The forecasting practice of 2022 continues, and 2023 supplies the outcomes.

- **13 February**, at maximum confidence: *"Ron DeSantis will absolutely NOT challenge Donald Trump in the 2024 Republican primary"*, with three tweets of reasoning about scorched-earth attacks and the popular-vote deficit. **DeSantis announced on 24 May 2023.** Recorded as **t016** in the testimony ledger and refuted.
- **24 May**, the same day: he does not pretend otherwise. *"Ron DeSantis is stupidly committing political suicide by moving ahead with a 2024 primary run"* — the prediction fails and the underlying analysis is restated as a judgement about the decision instead.
- **21 March**: *"There will be no charges filed against Trump this week"* and *"He will return to Twitter as a result of being indicted"* — the first correct, the second eventually so.
- **30 March**: *"I'm deeply embarrassed that I got tricked once again into believing that Donald Trump would be indicted. Fooled AGAIN by the fucking liberal mirage."*
- **13 June**: *"My official prediction is Trump eventually walks on all charges after a hung-jury mistrial."*

**The scoring behaviour is the finding, not the accuracy.** He states
predictions at explicit confidence, dates them, and when they fail he says so
in public and in his own voice — *"Fooled AGAIN"* — rather than quietly
dropping them. [[wiki/meta/testimony-veracity]] exists because most of Dan's
first-person claims cannot be checked; this is a seam of claims he built to be
checkable, and it is largely unmined.

## Texture

*"If you graduated high school with me and use Twitter, there's an
astronomically high probability that, in the last 12 hours, you've liked tweets
from both Ben Shapiro and Jordan Peterson"* (15 March) — the Uniontown cohort,
measured. An MLK assassination conspiracy studied *"as a pallet cleanser"*
(6 March). *"My first experience as the victim of an ageist attack"*
(21 February), at thirty-four. The Israel/Gaza posts from October are
sustained and take a position critical of the Israeli state, including an
argument that mandatory IDF service *"creates an automatic stain of
complicity"* — from someone the corpus records as having Jewish heritage on the
paternal line and no religion. And on **10 October**, the decision procedure
[[wiki/mind/politics/axioms]] already carries: *"Political positions are best
formulated and checked with one test: what would Michael Brooks do?"*

## What would change this reading

The Balloon Boy confirmation is the strongest thing here and it is six words —
strong because it is unprompted and specific, but six words. The AI reading
treats three scattered posts as a thread; they are genuinely scattered, and the
claim that the 2025 turn was continuous with them is an inference the 2025 and
2026 pages should be checked against rather than assumed. And the class-analysis
finding is about vocabulary arriving, which is the kind of claim the
`vocabulary-drift` lesson warns about from the other direction: the words are
new here, and it does not follow that the thoughts were absent before them.
